title: Review primary and accent usage outside standard QML Material components
scope: Backlog item only. Focus on whether custom and non-Material components use primary/accent colors sensibly. Analysis and implementation remain deferred.
request: Analyze whether the use of primary and accent colors in components outside QML Material controls is sensible and consistent.
expected: A component-level assessment of color roles, derivation, inheritance, and visual consistency outside standard Material controls, with justified recommendations where needed.
review_topics: Inventory primary/accent uses in custom components, plain QML items such as Rectangle, Text, and Canvas, and controls using another style.
Distinguish palette selections, resolved colors, Theme helper functions, and Material attached properties. Check that each use receives the intended value and theme context.
Assess whether primary/accent represents the right semantic role for each background, foreground, icon, highlight, border, and interaction state.
Check consistency with standard Material controls without assuming that every custom surface should use primary or accent.
Check reactive updates after changing primary/accent or Light, Dark, and System themes, including checked/inverse-theme states.
Evaluate foreground/background readability after opacity and background composition, not just the nominal color values.
Determine whether existing theme helpers are coherent or whether clearer shared color roles would improve consistency; do not assume a refactor is required.
implementation_notes: Use the broader color-role analysis from UX-001 and action-color conclusions from UX-002 where relevant instead of duplicating their work.
Inspect actual component bindings and rendered states. The presence of a Material color reference in a custom item is not by itself a defect.
Respect DESIGN.md's visual character and document intentional departures from standard controls.
Do not automatically replace custom components with Material controls or change their interaction design as part of this review.
Record any actionable implementation defects or proposed changes separately in the backlog.
acceptance_criteria: List the relevant custom/non-Material components and explain their current primary/accent usages.
Assess semantic appropriateness, theme propagation, readability, and consistency with the rest of the UI.
Identify intentional choices, verified defects, and optional improvements separately, with evidence for each recommendation.
Keep the output focused on custom/non-Material usage and link broader palette or action-color findings to UX-001/UX-002.
Make no implementation changes during the review alone.
evidence: Explicit user backlog request on 2026-10-28 to assess primary/accent usage in non-QML-Material components.
